subject: maths
title: Primary 4 Multiplying and Dividing Decimals
seo_title: P4 Multiplying and Dividing Decimals Worksheets: Free Primary 4 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: Multiplying and dividing decimals (up to 2 decimal places) by a 1-digit whole number; dividing whole numbers with quotient as a decimal; rounding answers
meta_desc: Free P4 maths practice: decimals × and ÷ a 1-digit number, 7 ÷ 4 = 1.75, rounding to 1 or 2 decimal places, money word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Work in tenths or hundredths, then check the decimal point with an estimate.
body_html:
Work in tenths and hundredths

Think of a decimal as a number of tenths or hundredths. 2.35 is 235 hundredths. Multiply or divide the whole number, then write the answer in the same unit. Estimate to check that the decimal point is in the right place.

Decimal × a 1-digit number

Split the decimal into its whole-number part and its decimal part. Multiply each part, then add.

Example 1

2.35 × 4

2.35 is 235 hundredths. 235 × 4 = 940, so 2.35 × 4 = 940 hundredths = 9.40. Estimate: 2 × 4 = 8, so 9.4 makes sense.

Answer: 9.4

Decimal ÷ a 1-digit number

Divide from the left, as with whole numbers. Put the decimal point in the answer straight above the decimal point in the number you divide. Rename what is left over: 2 ones = 20 tenths.

Example 2

4.08 ÷ 4

4 ones ÷ 4 = 1 one. 0 tenths ÷ 4 = 0 tenths. 8 hundredths ÷ 4 = 2 hundredths.

Answer: 1.02 (keep the 0 in the tenths place)

Whole number ÷ whole number as a decimal

Do not stop at the remainder. Write the whole number with zeros after a decimal point and keep dividing.

Rounding the answer

Some divisions never end: 10 ÷ 3 = 3.333… To round to 1 decimal place, look at the hundredths digit. To round to 2 decimal places, look at the thousandths digit. 5 or more: round up. Less than 5: keep it.

Word problems: draw a model

Example 3

Mrs Ng shares $10 equally among 3 children. How much does each child get, to the nearest cent?

$10 ÷ 3 = $3.333… The nearest cent is 2 decimal places. The thousandths digit is 3, so keep it.

Answer: $3.33

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
2.3 × 4 = 8.12 (writing 8 and 12 side by side)Add the parts: 8 + 1.2 = 9.2
2.35 × 4 = 8.35 (multiplying only the whole number)Multiply every digit: 9.4
7.2 ÷ 6 = 12 (leaving out the point)72 tenths ÷ 6 = 12 tenths = 1.2
4.08 ÷ 4 = 1.2 (dropping a zero)Keep the 0 that holds the tenths place: 1.02
7 ÷ 4 = 1 R 3 = 1.3 (remainder as decimal digits)Write 7 as 7.00 and keep dividing: 1.75
2 ÷ 3 ≈ 0.66 (cutting off digits)Look at the next digit: 0.666… ≈ 0.67

faq.q: What is taught in P4 multiplying and dividing decimals?
faq.a: In Primary 4, students multiply and divide decimals with up to 2 decimal places by a 1-digit whole number, such as 2.35 × 4 and 8.4 ÷ 3. They also divide whole numbers to get a decimal answer (7 ÷ 4 = 1.75) and round answers to 1 or 2 decimal places.

faq.q: How do I explain 7 ÷ 4 = 1.75 to my child?
faq.a: Tell your child not to stop at the remainder: write 7 as 7.00 and keep dividing. 3 ones left over make 30 tenths, 30 tenths ÷ 4 = 7 tenths with 2 tenths left, and 20 hundredths ÷ 4 = 5 hundredths, so 7 ÷ 4 = 1.75.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake?
faq.a: The most common mistake is putting the decimal point in the wrong place, for example 2.3 × 4 = 8.12 instead of 9.2, or writing the remainder as decimal digits (7 ÷ 4 = 1.3). Estimating first (2 × 4 = 8, so the answer is about 9) catches most of these.

faq.q: Is this in the MOE syllabus?
faq.a: Yes. Multiplying and dividing decimals by a 1-digit whole number, dividing whole numbers with a decimal quotient and rounding answers are part of the Primary 4 Decimals topic in the MOE 2021 Primary Mathematics Syllabus (Standard).

items.q: The number line shows 3 jumps of 0.4. What is 0.4 × 3?
items.e: 0.4 is 4 tenths. 4 × 3 = 12, so 0.4 × 3 = 12 tenths = 1.2. The red dot is 2 small marks past 1, at 1.2. 3.4 adds 3 + 0.4 instead of multiplying.

items.q: The number line shows 4 jumps of 0.6. What is 0.6 × 4?
items.e: 0.6 is 6 tenths. 6 × 4 = 24, so 0.6 × 4 = 24 tenths = 2.4. The red dot is 4 small marks past 2, at 2.4.
0.3 is 3 tenths. 3 × 2 = 6, so 0.3 × 2 = 6 tenths = 0.6. 0.06 is 6 hundredths, not 6 tenths.
0.7 is 7 tenths. 7 × 5 = 35, so 0.7 × 5 = 35 tenths = 3.5. 35 leaves out the decimal point. 5.7 adds instead of multiplying.
1.2 is 12 tenths. 12 × 3 = 36, so 1.2 × 3 = 36 tenths = 3.6. 4.2 adds 1.2 + 3 instead of multiplying.

items.q: The model splits 2.3 × 4 into 2 × 4 and 0.3 × 4. What is 2.3 × 4?
items.e: 2 × 4 = 8 and 0.3 × 4 = 1.2. Add the parts: 8 + 1.2 = 9.2. 8.12 writes 8 and 12 side by side instead of adding. 8.3 forgets to multiply the 0.3.

items.q: The model splits 3.6 × 2 into 3 × 2 and 0.6 × 2. What is 3.6 × 2?
items.e: 3 × 2 = 6 and 0.6 × 2 = 1.2. Add the parts: 6 + 1.2 = 7.2. 6.12 writes 6 and 12 side by side. 6.6 forgets to multiply the 0.6.
0.08 is 8 hundredths. 8 × 6 = 48, so 0.08 × 6 = 48 hundredths = 0.48. 4.8 is 48 tenths, but the answer is 48 hundredths.

2.35 is 235 hundredths. 235 × 4 = 940, so 2.35 × 4 = 940 hundredths = 9.4. 8.14 writes 2 × 4 = 8 and 0.35 × 4 = 1.4 side by side: add them, 8 + 1.4 = 9.4. Estimate: 2 × 4 = 8, so the answer is a bit more than 8.
4.5 is 45 tenths. 45 × 6 = 270, so 4.5 × 6 = 270 tenths = 27. 24.3 writes 4 × 6 = 24 and 0.5 × 6 = 3 side by side: add them, 24 + 3 = 27.
1.25 is 125 hundredths. 125 × 3 = 375, so 1.25 × 3 = 375 hundredths = 3.75. 4.25 adds 1.25 + 3 instead of multiplying.
0.45 is 45 hundredths. 45 × 7 = 315, so 0.45 × 7 = 315 hundredths = 3.15. 0.45 × 7 must be less than 7, so 31.5 cannot be right.
Use the inverse: 2.8 ÷ 4. 2.8 is 28 tenths, and 28 ÷ 4 = 7, so the answer is 7 tenths = 0.7. Check: 0.7 × 4 = 2.8. 11.2 is 2.8 × 4.
4.7 is 47 tenths, so the answer is 282 tenths = 28.2. Estimate: 5 × 6 = 30.
1.35 is 135 hundredths, so the answer is 945 hundredths = 9.45. Estimate: 1 × 7 = 7 and 2 × 7 = 14, so the answer is between 7 and 14.
3.08 is 308 hundredths. 308 × 5 = 1540, so 3.08 × 5 = 1540 hundredths = 15.4. 19 drops the 0 in the tenths place: it works out 3.8 × 5 instead of 3.08 × 5.
5.06 is 506 hundredths. 506 × 9 = 4554, so 5.06 × 9 = 4554 hundredths = 45.54. 50.4 drops the 0 in the tenths place: it works out 5.6 × 9. Estimate: 5 × 9 = 45.

items.q: Ali says 1.4 × 3 = 3.12. What is the correct answer?
items.e: 1 × 3 = 3 and 0.4 × 3 = 1.2. Ali wrote 3 and 12 side by side. Add the parts: 3 + 1.2 = 4.2.

items.q: Without working it out, between which two numbers is 3.8 × 7?
items.e: 3.8 is between 3 and 4, so 3.8 × 7 is between 3 × 7 = 21 and 4 × 7 = 28. In fact 3.8 × 7 = 26.6.
0.9 is 9 tenths. 9 ÷ 3 = 3, so 0.9 ÷ 3 = 3 tenths = 0.3. Check: 0.3 × 3 = 0.9. 2.7 multiplies instead of dividing.
4.8 is 48 tenths. 48 ÷ 4 = 12, so 4.8 ÷ 4 = 12 tenths = 1.2. Check: 1.2 × 4 = 4.8. 1.8 divides only the 4 ones and forgets the 8 tenths.
6.6 is 66 tenths. 66 ÷ 2 = 33, so 6.6 ÷ 2 = 33 tenths = 3.3. Check: 3.3 × 2 = 6.6. 13.2 multiplies instead of dividing.

8.4 is 84 tenths. 84 ÷ 3 = 28, so 8.4 ÷ 3 = 28 tenths = 2.8. Check: 2.8 × 3 = 8.4. In long division: 8 ones ÷ 3 = 2 ones R 2 ones. Rename 2 ones as 20 tenths: 20 + 4 = 24 tenths. 24 tenths ÷ 3 = 8 tenths.
2.4 is 24 tenths. 24 ÷ 8 = 3, so 2.4 ÷ 8 = 3 tenths = 0.3. Check: 0.3 × 8 = 2.4. 2.4 is less than 8, so the answer is less than 1.
3.5 is 35 tenths. 35 ÷ 7 = 5, so 3.5 ÷ 7 = 5 tenths = 0.5. Check: 0.5 × 7 = 3.5. 2 is 7 ÷ 3.5: it divides the wrong way round. 3.5 is less than 7, so the answer is less than 1.
9.6 is 96 tenths. 96 ÷ 4 = 24, so 9.6 ÷ 4 = 24 tenths = 2.4. Check: 2.4 × 4 = 9.6. Estimate: 8 ÷ 4 = 2, so the answer is a bit more than 2.

items.q: Hui Min says 7.2 ÷ 6 = 12. What is the correct answer?
items.e: 7.2 is 72 tenths. 72 ÷ 6 = 12, so 7.2 ÷ 6 = 12 tenths = 1.2. Estimate: 6 ÷ 6 = 1, so the answer is about 1, not about 12. Hui Min left out the decimal point.
13.5 is 135 tenths. 135 ÷ 9 = 15, so 13.5 ÷ 9 = 15 tenths = 1.5. Check: 1.5 × 9 = 13.5. Estimate: 9 ÷ 9 = 1 and 18 ÷ 9 = 2, so the answer is between 1 and 2.
16.2 is 162 tenths. 162 ÷ 6 = 27, so 16.2 ÷ 6 = 27 tenths = 2.7. Check: 2.7 × 6 = 16.2. Estimate: 18 ÷ 6 = 3, so the answer is a bit less than 3.
4.08 is 408 hundredths. 408 ÷ 4 = 102, so 4.08 ÷ 4 = 102 hundredths = 1.02. Check: 1.02 × 4 = 4.08. 1.2 drops the 0 that holds the tenths place: 0 tenths ÷ 4 is 0 tenths, so write 0.
6.18 is 618 hundredths. 618 ÷ 6 = 103, so 6.18 ÷ 6 = 103 hundredths = 1.03. Check: 1.03 × 6 = 6.18. 1.3 drops the 0 that holds the tenths place: 1 tenth ÷ 6 is 0 tenths R 1 tenth, so write 0.
0.72 is 72 hundredths. 72 ÷ 9 = 8, so 0.72 ÷ 9 = 8 hundredths = 0.08. Check: 0.08 × 9 = 0.72. 0.8 is 8 tenths, but the answer is 8 hundredths.
8.55 is 855 hundredths. 855 ÷ 5 = 171, so 8.55 ÷ 5 = 171 hundredths = 1.71. Check: 1.71 × 5 = 8.55. Estimate: 10 ÷ 5 = 2, so the answer is a bit less than 2. 42.75 multiplies by 5.
9.24 is 924 hundredths. 924 ÷ 4 = 231, so 9.24 ÷ 4 = 231 hundredths = 2.31. Check: 2.31 × 4 = 9.24. Estimate: 8 ÷ 4 = 2, so the answer is a bit more than 2. 36.96 multiplies by 4.

items.q: The quotient digits for 8.52 ÷ 4 are 2, 1, 3. Where does the decimal point go?
items.e: Put the decimal point in the quotient straight above the point in 8.52. Estimate: 8 ÷ 4 = 2, so the answer is about 2. 8.52 ÷ 4 = 2.13.

items.q: The quotient digits for 6.95 ÷ 5 are 1, 3, 9. What is 6.95 ÷ 5?
items.e: The point in the quotient goes straight above the point in 6.95. Estimate: 5 ÷ 5 = 1 and 10 ÷ 5 = 2, so the answer is between 1 and 2. 6.95 ÷ 5 = 1.39. Check: 1.39 × 5 = 6.95.

Write 4.5 as 4.50. 4.50 is 450 hundredths. 450 ÷ 2 = 225, so 4.5 ÷ 2 = 225 hundredths = 2.25. Check: 2.25 × 2 = 4.5. 2.2 stops too early: 4.5 ÷ 2 = 2.2 R 0.1. 2.21 writes the remainder 1 as a digit. Rename the 1 tenth left over as 10 hundredths and keep dividing: 10 hundredths ÷ 2 = 5 hundredths.

items.q: 7.35 is 735 hundredths. What is 735 hundredths ÷ 5?
items.e: 735 ÷ 5 = 147, and the unit stays the same: 147 hundredths = 1.47. So 7.35 ÷ 5 = 1.47.

items.q: Which answer is less than 1?
items.e: The answer is less than 1 when the number you divide is less than the number you divide by. Only 5.6 is less than 8, so only 5.6 ÷ 8 is less than 1 (it is 0.7).

sets.title: Whole numbers ÷ a 1-digit number: answers as decimals

items.e: 9 ÷ 2 = 4 R 1. Do not stop at the remainder: write 9 as 9.0 and keep dividing. The 1 one left over makes 10 tenths. 9 ÷ 2 = 4.5. Check: 4.5 × 2 = 9. 4.1 writes the remainder 1 as a decimal digit.

1 ÷ 2 = 0 R 1. Do not stop at the remainder: write 1 as 1.0 and keep dividing. The 1 one left over makes 10 tenths. 1 ÷ 2 = 0.5. Check: 0.5 × 2 = 1. 0.1 writes the remainder 1 as a decimal digit. 2 divides the wrong way round.
6 ÷ 5 = 1 R 1. Do not stop at the remainder: write 6 as 6.0 and keep dividing. The 1 one left over makes 10 tenths. 6 ÷ 5 = 1.2. Check: 1.2 × 5 = 6. 1.1 writes the remainder 1 as a decimal digit.

3 ÷ 4 = 0 R 3. Do not stop at the remainder: write 3 as 3.00 and keep dividing. The 3 ones left over make 30 tenths. 3 ÷ 4 = 0.75. Check: 0.75 × 4 = 3. 3 is less than 4, so the answer is less than 1. 0.3 writes the remainder 3 as a decimal digit.

items.q: To find 7 ÷ 4, Siti writes 7 as 7.00. The quotient digits are 1, 7, 5. What is 7 ÷ 4?
items.e: 7 ÷ 4 = 1 R 3. Do not stop at the remainder: write 7 as 7.00 and keep dividing. The 3 ones left over make 30 tenths. 7 ÷ 4 = 1.75. Check: 1.75 × 4 = 7. 1.3 writes the remainder 3 as a decimal digit. The point in the quotient goes straight above the point in 7.00.

13 ÷ 5 = 2 R 3. Do not stop at the remainder: write 13 as 13.0 and keep dividing. The 3 ones left over make 30 tenths. 13 ÷ 5 = 2.6. Check: 2.6 × 5 = 13. 2.3 writes the remainder 3 as a decimal digit.
3 ÷ 5 = 0 R 3. Do not stop at the remainder: write 3 as 3.0 and keep dividing. The 3 ones left over make 30 tenths. 3 ÷ 5 = 0.6. Check: 0.6 × 5 = 3. 0.3 writes the remainder 3 as a decimal digit.
9 ÷ 6 = 1 R 3. Do not stop at the remainder: write 9 as 9.0 and keep dividing. The 3 ones left over make 30 tenths. 9 ÷ 6 = 1.5. Check: 1.5 × 6 = 9. 1.3 writes the remainder 3 as a decimal digit.

11 ÷ 4 = 2 R 3. Do not stop at the remainder: write 11 as 11.00 and keep dividing. The 3 ones left over make 30 tenths. 11 ÷ 4 = 2.75. Check: 2.75 × 4 = 11. 2.3 writes the remainder 3 as a decimal digit.
9 ÷ 4 = 2 R 1. Do not stop at the remainder: write 9 as 9.00 and keep dividing. The 1 one left over makes 10 tenths. 9 ÷ 4 = 2.25. Check: 2.25 × 4 = 9. 2.1 writes the remainder 1 as a decimal digit.

27 ÷ 6 = 4 R 3. Do not stop at the remainder: write 27 as 27.0 and keep dividing. The 3 ones left over make 30 tenths. 27 ÷ 6 = 4.5. Check: 4.5 × 6 = 27. 4.3 writes the remainder 3 as a decimal digit.

19 ÷ 4 = 4 R 3. Do not stop at the remainder: write 19 as 19.00 and keep dividing. The 3 ones left over make 30 tenths. 19 ÷ 4 = 4.75. Check: 4.75 × 4 = 19. 4.3 writes the remainder 3 as a decimal digit.

items.q: 13 ÷ 4 is written as 13.00 ÷ 4. The quotient digits are 3, 2, 5. Where does the decimal point go?
items.e: The point in the quotient goes straight above the point in 13.00. Estimate: 12 ÷ 4 = 3, so the answer is about 3. 13 ÷ 4 = 3.25.

30 ÷ 8 = 3 R 6. Do not stop at the remainder: write 30 as 30.00 and keep dividing. The 6 ones left over make 60 tenths. 30 ÷ 8 = 3.75. Check: 3.75 × 8 = 30. 3.6 writes the remainder 6 as a decimal digit.

items.q: 5 ÷ 4 = 1 R 1. Kumar writes 5 ÷ 4 = 1.1. What is the correct answer?
items.e: 5 ÷ 4 = 1 R 1. Do not stop at the remainder: write 5 as 5.00 and keep dividing. The 1 one left over makes 10 tenths. 5 ÷ 4 = 1.25. Check: 1.25 × 4 = 5. Kumar wrote the remainder 1 as a decimal digit. 1.4 reads 1 quarter as 0.4.

items.q: 14 = 1 ÷ 4. Write 14 as a decimal.
items.e: 1 ÷ 4: write 1 as 1.00. 100 hundredths ÷ 4 = 25 hundredths, so 14 = 0.25. 0.4 and 0.14 copy the digits of the fraction. 4 is 4 ÷ 1.

items.q: 25 = 2 ÷ 5. Write 25 as a decimal.
items.e: 2 ÷ 5: write 2 as 2.0. 20 tenths ÷ 5 = 4 tenths, so 25 = 0.4. 2.5 is 5 ÷ 2: it divides the wrong way round. 0.25 copies the digits. 0.2 uses only the 2.

items.q: Which division has the answer 2.5?

items.e: 21 ÷ 4 = 5 R 1. Do not stop at the remainder: write 21 as 21.00 and keep dividing. The 1 one left over makes 10 tenths. 21 ÷ 4 = 5.25. Check: 5.25 × 4 = 21. 5.1 writes the remainder 1 as a decimal digit. 5.4 reads 1 quarter as 0.4, but 1 quarter = 0.25.

items.q: Which is the same as 15 ÷ 4?
items.e: 15 ÷ 4 = 3 R 3. Do not stop at the remainder: write 15 as 15.00 and keep dividing. The 3 ones left over make 30 tenths. 15 ÷ 4 = 3.75. Check: 3.75 × 4 = 15. 3.3 writes the remainder 3 as a decimal digit. 3.4 is 3 and 4 tenths, not 3 and 3 quarters.

sets.title: Rounding answers to 1 or 2 decimal places

items.q: The arrow is at 2.67. Round 2.67 to 1 decimal place.
items.e: To round to 1 decimal place, look at the hundredths digit of 2.67: it is 7. It is 5 or more, so round the tenths digit up. 2.67 ≈ 2.7. 2.6 cuts off the 7 instead of rounding. On the number line, 2.67 is nearer to 2.7 than to 2.6.

items.q: The arrow is at 4.32. Round 4.32 to 1 decimal place.
items.e: To round to 1 decimal place, look at the hundredths digit of 4.32: it is 2. It is less than 5, so the tenths digit stays the same. 4.32 ≈ 4.3. 4.32 is before the half-way mark 4.35, so it is nearer to 4.3.

items.q: Round 5.48 to 1 decimal place.
items.e: To round to 1 decimal place, look at the hundredths digit of 5.48: it is 8. It is 5 or more, so round the tenths digit up. 5.48 ≈ 5.5. 5.4 cuts off the 8 instead of rounding. 5 rounds to the nearest whole number.

items.q: Round 3.456 to 2 decimal places.
items.e: To round to 2 decimal places, look at the thousandths digit of 3.456: it is 6. It is 5 or more, so round the hundredths digit up. 3.456 ≈ 3.46. 3.45 cuts off the 6. 3.5 is rounded to 1 decimal place, not 2.

items.q: Round 7.249 to 1 decimal place.
items.e: To round to 1 decimal place, look at the hundredths digit of 7.249: it is 4. It is less than 5, so the tenths digit stays the same. 7.249 ≈ 7.2. 7.3 rounds twice (7.249 → 7.25 → 7.3). Only look at the hundredths digit, 4.

items.q: Round 0.95 to 1 decimal place.
items.e: To round to 1 decimal place, look at the hundredths digit of 0.95: it is 5. It is 5 or more, so round the tenths digit up. 0.95 ≈ 1.0. 9 tenths + 1 tenth = 10 tenths = 1 whole, so the answer is 1.0. Write the 0 to show 1 decimal place.

items.q: Round 12.051 to 2 decimal places.
items.e: To round to 2 decimal places, look at the thousandths digit of 12.051: it is 1. It is less than 5, so the hundredths digit stays the same. 12.051 ≈ 12.05. 12.06 rounds up even though the next digit is only 1. 12.5 drops the 0 in the tenths place.

items.q: The arrow is at 5.136. Round 5.136 to 2 decimal places.
items.e: To round to 2 decimal places, look at the thousandths digit of 5.136: it is 6. It is 5 or more, so round the hundredths digit up. 5.136 ≈ 5.14. 5.136 is past the half-way mark 5.135, so it is nearer to 5.14.

items.q: 10 ÷ 3 = 3.333… Round the answer to 1 decimal place.
items.e: To round to 1 decimal place, look at the hundredths digit of 3.333…: it is 3. It is less than 5, so the tenths digit stays the same. 3.333… ≈ 3.3. 3.33 is rounded to 2 decimal places, not 1.

items.q: Find 10 ÷ 3. Round your answer to 2 decimal places.
items.e: To round to 2 decimal places, look at the thousandths digit of 3.333…: it is 3. It is less than 5, so the hundredths digit stays the same. 3.333… ≈ 3.33. 10 ÷ 3 = 3 R 1, so 3.1 writes the remainder as a digit. Divide to 3 decimal places (3.333), then round.

items.q: Find 2 ÷ 3. Round your answer to 2 decimal places.
items.e: To round to 2 decimal places, look at the thousandths digit of 0.666…: it is 6. It is 5 or more, so round the hundredths digit up. 0.666… ≈ 0.67. 0.66 cuts off the digits instead of rounding. 1.5 is 3 ÷ 2.

items.q: Find 5 ÷ 3. Round your answer to 1 decimal place.
items.e: To round to 1 decimal place, look at the hundredths digit of 1.66…: it is 6. It is 5 or more, so round the tenths digit up. 1.66… ≈ 1.7. 1.6 cuts off the digits. 1.2 writes the remainder 2 as a digit. 0.6 is 3 ÷ 5.

items.q: Find 7 ÷ 6. Round your answer to 1 decimal place.
items.e: To round to 1 decimal place, look at the hundredths digit of 1.16…: it is 6. It is 5 or more, so round the tenths digit up. 1.16… ≈ 1.2. 1.1 cuts off the digits (or writes the remainder 1 as a digit). 1.17 is rounded to 2 decimal places.

items.q: Find 8 ÷ 7. Round your answer to 2 decimal places.
items.e: To round to 2 decimal places, look at the thousandths digit of 1.142…: it is 2. It is less than 5, so the hundredths digit stays the same. 1.142… ≈ 1.14. 0.88 is 7 ÷ 8, which divides the wrong way round.

items.q: Find 4.7 ÷ 3. Round your answer to 2 decimal places.
items.e: To round to 2 decimal places, look at the thousandths digit of 1.566…: it is 6. It is 5 or more, so round the hundredths digit up. 1.566… ≈ 1.57. 1.56 cuts off the digits. 14.1 multiplies instead of dividing.

items.q: Find 5.2 ÷ 6. Round your answer to 1 decimal place.
items.e: To round to 1 decimal place, look at the hundredths digit of 0.86…: it is 6. It is 5 or more, so round the tenths digit up. 0.86… ≈ 0.9. 0.8 cuts off the digits. 0.87 is rounded to 2 decimal places.

items.q: Find 0.85 × 3. Round your answer to 1 decimal place.
items.e: To round to 1 decimal place, look at the hundredths digit of 2.55: it is 5. It is 5 or more, so round the tenths digit up. 2.55 ≈ 2.6. 0.85 × 3 = 2.55 exactly. 2.5 cuts off the 5 instead of rounding. 3 is rounded to the nearest whole number.

items.q: Which number is 4.3 when it is rounded to 1 decimal place?
items.e: 4.26 → look at the hundredths digit, 6: round up to 4.3. 4.35 and 4.36 round to 4.4. 4.24 rounds to 4.2.

items.q: Mrs Ng shares $10 equally among 3 children. How much does each child get, to the nearest cent?
items.e: $10 ÷ 3 = $3.333… To the nearest cent means to 2 decimal places. The thousandths digit is 3, so the hundredths digit stays: $3.33. $3.10 writes the remainder 1 as a digit. $3.30 is rounded to 1 decimal place.

items.q: Mr Tan shares $50 equally among 7 people. How much does each person get, to the nearest cent?
items.e: $50 ÷ 7 = $7.142… The thousandths digit is 2, so the hundredths digit stays: $7.14. $7.10 writes the remainder 1 as a digit. $71.40 puts the decimal point in the wrong place.

sets.title: Word problems with money and measures

items.q: Three friends share $25.50 equally. How much money does each friend get?
items.e: 3 units = $25.50, so 1 unit = $25.50 ÷ 3 = $8.50. 2550¢ ÷ 3 = 850¢. $76.50 multiplies by 3 instead of dividing.

items.q: Mei Ling buys 4 curry puffs at the school canteen. Each curry puff costs $1.40. How much does she pay?
items.e: 4 units = $1.40 × 4 = $5.60. 140¢ × 4 = 560¢. $5.40 adds 4 instead of multiplying.

items.q: Mrs Ng pays $1.25 for each bus ride with her EZ-Link card. She takes 6 bus rides in a week. How much does she pay in all?
items.e: 1.25 × 6: 125 hundredths × 6 = 750 hundredths = $7.50. $7.25 adds 6 instead of multiplying.

items.q: A ribbon 4.8 m long is cut into 6 equal pieces. How long is each piece?
items.e: 6 units = 4.8 m. 4.8 is 48 tenths. 48 ÷ 6 = 8, so 1 unit = 8 tenths = 0.8 m. 8 m is longer than the whole ribbon.

items.q: Mr Tan pays $13.50 for 3 plates of chicken rice at a hawker centre. Each plate costs the same. How much does 1 plate cost?
items.e: 1 unit = $13.50 ÷ 3. 13 ÷ 3 = 4 R 1. Rename 1 one as 10 tenths: 10 + 5 = 15 tenths, and 15 tenths ÷ 3 = 5 tenths. So 1 plate costs $4.50. $4.05 puts the 5 in the wrong place.

items.q: Siti saves $2.75 every week. How much does she save in 8 weeks?
items.e: 2.75 × 8: 275 hundredths × 8 = 2200 hundredths = $22. Check: 2 × 8 = 16 and 0.75 × 8 = 6, so 16 + 6 = 22. $16.75 multiplies only the dollars.

items.q: Raju buys 3 bottles of water for Sports Day. Each bottle holds 1.5 ℓ. How much water is there in all?
items.e: 1.5 × 3 = 15 tenths × 3 = 45 tenths = 4.5 ℓ. 3.15 ℓ writes 1 × 3 = 3 and 0.5 × 3 = 1.5 side by side instead of adding.

items.q: Kumar runs 2.4 km at East Coast Park every day. How far does he run in 5 days?
items.e: 2.4 × 5 = 24 tenths × 5 = 120 tenths = 12 km. 10.4 km multiplies only the 2 and forgets the 0.4.

items.q: Mrs Lim cuts a 7 m rope into 4 equal pieces. How long is each piece?
items.e: 4 units = 7 m, so 1 unit = 7 ÷ 4. 7 ÷ 4 = 1 R 3. Write 7 as 7.00 and keep dividing: 7 ÷ 4 = 1.75 m. 1.3 m writes the remainder 3 as a decimal digit.

items.q: Mdm Wong pays $9 for 4 kg of rambutans. What is the cost of 1 kg?
items.e: $9 ÷ 4 = 2 R 1. Write 9 as 9.00 and keep dividing: 9 ÷ 4 = 2.25, so 1 kg costs $2.25. $2.10 writes the remainder 1 as a digit. $36 multiplies.

items.q: A cup of bubble tea costs $3.80. Chloe buys 3 cups for her family. How much does she pay?
Priya walks 0.65 km from her HDB block to school every morning. How far does she walk to school in 5 days?
items.e: 0.65 × 5 = 65 hundredths × 5 = 325 hundredths = 3.25 km. 5.65 km adds instead of multiplying.

items.q: Mr Rahman pays $27.60 for 6 kg of durians. What is the cost of 1 kg?
items.e: $27.60 ÷ 6: 2760¢ ÷ 6 = 460¢ = $4.60. Estimate: $30 ÷ 6 = $5. $4.06 puts the 6 in the hundredths place instead of the tenths place.

items.q: Kavya pours 2.4 ℓ of orange juice equally into 8 cups. How much juice is in each cup?
items.e: 2.4 ÷ 8 = 24 tenths ÷ 8 = 3 tenths = 0.3 ℓ. 3 ℓ is more than the whole 2.4 ℓ.

items.q: Ryan pours 10 ℓ of water equally into 6 pails. How much water is in each pail? Round your answer to 1 decimal place.
items.e: 10 ÷ 6 = 1.66… The hundredths digit is 6, so round up: 1.7 ℓ. 1.6 ℓ cuts off the digits. 1.4 ℓ writes the remainder 4 as a digit. 0.6 ℓ is 6 ÷ 10.

items.q: Ahmad shares $20 equally among 3 friends. How much does each friend get, to the nearest cent?
items.e: $20 ÷ 3 = $6.666… To the nearest cent means 2 decimal places. The thousandths digit is 6, so round up: $6.67. $6.66 cuts off the digits. $6.20 writes the remainder 2 as a digit.

items.q: Ethan’s pencil case costs $4.65. Sarah’s pencil case costs 3 times as much. How much more does Sarah’s pencil case cost than Ethan’s?
items.e: Sarah has 2 more units than Ethan. 2 units = $4.65 × 2 = $9.30. $13.95 is the cost of Sarah’s pencil case, not the difference. $18.60 is the total of both. $1.55 divides by 3.

items.q: Raju and 3 friends share the cost of a $15.20 birthday cake equally. How much does each of them pay?
items.e: Raju and 3 friends are 4 people, so 4 units = $15.20. 1 unit = $15.20 ÷ 4 = $3.80. $5.07 divides by 3 and forgets Raju. $60.80 multiplies.

items.q: Nurul buys 3 files at $1.65 each. She pays with a $10 note. How much change does she get?
items.e: Cost: 1.65 × 3 = $4.95. Change: $10.00 − $4.95 = $5.05. $4.95 is the cost, not the change. $8.35 forgets to multiply by 3. $6.05 forgets to rename a dollar when subtracting.

items.q: Zhi Hao has $18.50. He buys 3 notebooks at $2.85 each. How much money does he have left?
items.e: Cost: 2.85 × 3 = 285¢ × 3 = 855¢ = $8.55. Left: $18.50 − $8.55 = $9.95. $8.55 is the cost, not the money left. $15.65 forgets to multiply by 3. $10.95 forgets to rename when subtracting.
